paired.name: paired-fresh-estimators
paired.head: 6e9f018b0c619999a3822856ce655ca701d47411
paired.title: Use independent estimator fits in paired statistical comparisons
paired.body:
### Description

The four paired estimator-comparison helpers fit the same estimator objects repeatedly. Estimators that retain fitted state, including random forests with `warm_start=True`, can therefore reuse trees trained on an earlier split. A later test fold may already have influenced those trees, changing both the comparison statistic and its p-value.

This change clones each estimator before each independent fit in `paired_ttest_resampled`, `paired_ttest_kfold_cv`, `paired_ttest_5x2cv`, and `combined_ftest_5x2cv`. Scoring uses the fitted clones, and the supplied estimators retain their original state. The sampling, scoring, and statistical formulas stay the same. All four entry points share this cause and are covered together.

### Related issues or pull requests

Closes #1318.

Related work: #1242 adds a separate corrected resampled t-test; it does not change these existing four helpers. #1315 isolates bootstrap models in the separate `bias_variance_decomp` path. This PR addresses the independent repeated train/test fits above. Deduplication examined upstream PR refs, all fork heads, and their reachable intermediate changes to both source files; no equivalent change to these four entry points was found.

### Validation

- Exact upstream base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`.
- **23 of 28 new regression cases fail on unchanged source.** All 28 pass after the change.
- The tests compare real warm-start random forests with independently fitted models and separately computed test statistics. They cover regression and classification, pipelines, already-fitted inputs, cold-start controls, callable scoring, and unchanged caller state. A state-tracking estimator also verifies that the scorer never sees training observations retained from another fold.
- Existing and new tests for the four helpers: **41 passed**. Complete repository suite: **768 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Baseline and candidate ran in the same job using Python 3.11.18 and the unchanged frozen dependency lock.
- Complete repository isort/Black, changed-file Flake8, `git diff --check`, package build, and strict Twine metadata checks passed. The repository-wide Flake8 report retains existing findings and is not claimed as a clean lint gate.

[Baseline reproduction and complete validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43881707255/job/133348986775).

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added regression tests in the corresponding test directory.
- [x] Updated the affected public docstrings.
- [x] Ran focused and complete repository tests.
- [x] Checked formatting and style with the scope described above.

bootstrap_issue.title: bootstrap reports infinite or zero standard error for finite rescaled statistics
bootstrap_issue.body:
#### Describe the bug

`bootstrap` computes the standard deviation of the replicate statistics directly. Squaring finite deviations can overflow or underflow even when the standard error itself is representable. Consequently, changing the units of an otherwise identical sample can change a finite, nonzero standard error into infinity or zero.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import numpy as np
from mlxtend.evaluate import bootstrap

for scale in (1.0, 1e200, 1e-200):
    original, se, interval = bootstrap(
        np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0]) * scale,
        np.mean, num_rounds=50, seed=7,
    )
    print(scale, original, se, interval)
```

#### Expected Results

The unscaled standard error is approximately 0.7793410350928481. The other two standard errors should be approximately 7.793410350928481e199 and 7.793410350928481e-201. All are finite and nonzero. The original statistic and percentile interval already remain finite in this example.

#### Actual Results

The standard errors are approximately 0.7793410350928481, `inf`, and `0.0`.

#### Proposed correction

Scale finite replicate statistics by an exact power of two before computing their standard deviation, then restore the scale afterward. Preserve the existing resampling, percentile convention, degrees of freedom, and propagation of nonfinite statistics. Regression tests should compare with a separate high-precision variance calculation and cover large, small, ordinary, and constant statistics.

The complete reachable history for `mlxtend/evaluate/bootstrap.py` contains 45 commits and 17 distinct source versions. All versions use the same direct `np.std(bootstrap_replicates, ddof=ddof)` calculation; no equivalent correction was found.

#### Versions

Current master `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`, Linux, Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0, scikit-learn 1.8.0.

official_format_notes.note:
### Official formatting CI follow-up

The [official formatting job](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/actions/runs/43877679562/job/133334889646) fails while installing its dependencies, before running style checks. Its `python-version: 3.x` selects Python 3.15.2; the locked SciPy 1.16.3 source build then reports `Dependency "OpenBLAS" not found`. The [unchanged upstream base reproduces the same installation failure](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43867750166/job/133300579092). Complete repository isort/Black and changed-file Flake8 passed under the frozen Python 3.11 validation linked above. Both official functional jobs now pass: [locked dependencies](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/actions/runs/43877679729/job/133334890507) and [latest scikit-learn](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/actions/runs/43877679729/job/133334890169).
